sanskrit: saptadhā tu kṛte garbhe ditiḥ paramaduḥkhitā sahasrākṣaṃ durādharṣaṃ vākyaṃ sānunayābravīt
english: When her womb had been split into seven parts, Diti, deeply grieved, spoke words of supplication to the thousand-eyed Indra, that invincible one.

sanskrit: mamāparādhād garbho 'yaṃ saptadhā viphalīkṛtaḥ nāparādho 'sti deveśa tavātra balasūdana
english: Through my own transgression this embryo has been destroyed and split into seven; there is no fault in you in this matter, O lord of the gods, O slayer of Bala.

sanskrit: priyaṃ tu kṛtam icchāmi mama garbhaviparyaye marutāṃ saptaṃ saptānāṃ sthānapālā bhavantv ime
english: Yet I desire that something favorable be done for me in the ruin of my womb: let these seven become the guardians of seven regions as the Maruts.

sanskrit: vātaskandhā ime sapta carantu divi putrakāḥ mārutā iti vikhyātā divyarūpā mamātmajāḥ
english: Let these seven, bearers of the wind, roam heaven as my sons — known as the Mārutas, of divine form, my own children.

sanskrit: brahmalokaṃ caratv eka indralokaṃ tathāparaḥ divi vāyur iti khyātas tṛtīyo 'pi mahāyaśāḥ
english: Let one roam the world of Brahmā, and another the world of Indra; let a third, of great renown, be known in heaven as Vāyu.

sanskrit: catvāras tu suraśreṣṭha diśo vai tava śāsanāt saṃcariṣyanti bhadraṃ te devabhūtā mamātmajāḥ tvatkṛtenaiva nāmnā ca mārutā iti viśrutāḥ
english: And may four, O foremost of gods, roam the four directions by your command — may all be well with you; my sons, become divine beings, shall be renowned as the Mārutas by the very name you have bestowed.

sanskrit: tasyās tad vacanaṃ śrutvā sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ uvāca prāñjalir vākyaṃ ditiṃ balaniṣūdanaḥ
english: Having heard her words, the thousand-eyed Indra, the destroyer of citadels, the slayer of Bala, spoke these words to Diti with joined palms.

sanskrit: sarvam etad yathoktaṃ te bhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ vicariṣyanti bhadraṃ te devabhūtās tavātmajāḥ
english: All that you have said shall come to pass — there is no doubt. May it be well with you; your sons, having become divine beings, shall roam as you wish.

sanskrit: evaṃ tau niścayaṃ kṛtvā mātāputrau tapovane jagmatus tridivaṃ rāma kṛtārthāv iti naḥ śrutam
english: Having thus come to this resolution, O Rāma, the mother and son, their purpose accomplished, departed from that ascetic forest to the three heavens — so we have heard.

sanskrit: eṣa deśaḥ sa kākutstha mahendrādhyuṣitaḥ purā ditiṃ yatra tapaḥ siddhām evaṃ paricacāra saḥ
english: This is the very region, O descendant of Kākutstha, once inhabited by Mahendra, where he thus attended upon Diti who had achieved the fruit of her austerity.

sanskrit: ikṣvākos tu naravyāghra putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ alambuṣāyām utpanno viśāla iti viśrutaḥ
english: Of Ikṣvāku, O tiger among men, there was born a most righteous son, born of Alambuṣā, renowned by the name Viśālā.

sanskrit: tena cāsīd iha sthāne viśāleti purī kṛtā
english: By him was the city named Viśālā established here in this very place.

sanskrit: viśālasya suto rāma hemacandro mahābalaḥ sucandra iti vikhyāto hemacandrād anantaraḥ
english: The son of Viśālā, O Rāma, was Hemacandra, of great might; Sucandra, next after Hemacandra, was renowned by that name.

sanskrit: sucandratanayo rāma dhūmrāśva iti viśrutaḥ dhūmrāśvatanayaś cāpi sṛñjayaḥ samapadyata
english: The son of Sucandra, O Rāma, was known as Dhūmrāśva; and from Dhūmrāśva there arose a son called Sṛñjaya.

sanskrit: sṛñjayasya sutaḥ śrīmān sahadevaḥ pratāpavān kuśāśvaḥ sahadevasya putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ
english: The glorious and valiant son of Sṛñjaya was Sahadeva; and Kuśāśva, most devoted to righteousness, was the son of Sahadeva.

sanskrit: kuśāśvasya mahātejāḥ somadattaḥ pratāpavān somadattasya putras tu kākutstha iti viśrutaḥ
english: Of Kuśāśva was born Somadatta, of great splendor and valor; and the son of Somadatta, O descendant of Kākutstha, is renowned as such.

sanskrit: tasya putro mahātejāḥ saṃpraty eṣa purīm imām āvasaty amaraprakhyaḥ sumatir nāma durjayaḥ
english: His son, of great splendor, resembling an immortal, named Sumati, the unconquerable, now inhabits this city.

sanskrit: ikṣvākos tu prasādena sarve vaiśālikā nṛpāḥ dīrghāyuṣo mahātmāno vīryavantaḥ sudhārmikāḥ
english: By the grace of Ikṣvāku, all the kings of Viśālā are long-lived, great-souled, heroic, and deeply righteous.

sanskrit: ihādya rajanīṃ rāma sukhaṃ vatsyāmahe vayam śvaḥ prabhāte naraśreṣṭha janakaṃ draṣṭum arhasi
english: Here today, O Rāma, let us pass the night in comfort; at tomorrow's dawn, O best of men, you should visit King Janaka.

sanskrit: sumatis tu mahātejā viśvāmitram upāgatam śrutvā naravaraśreṣṭhaḥ pratyudgacchan mahāyaśāḥ
english: The greatly splendid Sumati, foremost among excellent men, of great renown, having heard of Viśvāmitra's arrival, went forth to meet him.

sanskrit: pūjāṃ ca paramāṃ kṛtvā sopādhyāyaḥ sabāndhavaḥ prāñjaliḥ kuśalaṃ pṛṣṭvā viśvāmitram athābravīt
english: Having offered the highest honor together with his teachers and kinsmen, with joined palms, inquiring after his welfare, he then spoke to Viśvāmitra.

sanskrit: dhanyo 'smy anugṛhīto 'smi yasya me viṣayaṃ mune saṃprāpto darśanaṃ caiva nāsti dhanyataro mama
english: I am blessed, I am honored, O sage, that you have arrived in my domain and that I have your audience — there is none more blessed than I.

sanskrit: pṛṣṭvā tu kuśalaṃ tatra parasparasamāgame kathānte sumatir vākyaṃ vyājahāra mahāmunim
english: Having inquired after each other's welfare at that mutual meeting, Sumati, at the conclusion of their conversation, addressed the great sage.

sanskrit: imau kumārau bhadraṃ te devatulyaparākramau gajasiṃhagatī vīrau śārdūlavṛṣabhopamau
english: May all be well with you — these two princes, whose valor equals that of the gods, who move like elephant and lion, who are compared to a tiger and a bull,

sanskrit: padmapatraviśālākṣau khaḍgatūṇīdhanurdharau aśvināv iva rūpeṇa samupasthitayauvanau
english: With wide eyes like lotus petals, bearing sword, quiver, and bow, like the twin Aśvins in form, their youth just come to fullness —

sanskrit: yadṛcchayaiva gāṃ prāptau devalokād ivāmarau kathaṃ padbhyām iha prāptau kimarthaṃ kasya vā mune
english: Who have come to earth as if by chance, like immortals descended from the world of gods — how have they come here on foot, O sage, for what purpose, and whose sons are they?

sanskrit: bhūṣayantāv imaṃ deśaṃ candrasūryāv ivāmbaram parasparasya sadṛśau pramāṇeṅgitaceṣṭitaiḥ
english: They adorn this region as the sun and moon adorn the sky, similar to each other in measure, bearing, and conduct.

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca naraśreṣṭhau saṃprāptau durgame pathi varāyudhadharau vīrau śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: For what purpose have these two foremost of men arrived by so difficult a road, bearing the finest of weapons, these two heroes? I desire to hear the truth of it.

sanskrit: tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayat siddhāśramanivāsaṃ ca rākṣasānāṃ vadhaṃ tathā
english: Having heard his words, Viśvāmitra reported to him what had happened: their stay at Siddhāśrama, and the slaying of the Rākṣasas.

sanskrit: viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā rājā paramaharṣitaḥ atithī paramau prāptau putrau daśarathasya tau pūjayām āsa vidhivat satkārārhau mahābalau
english: Hearing Viśvāmitra's account, the king was filled with the greatest joy; those two most excellent guests who had arrived — the sons of Daśaratha, those two of great strength worthy of honor — he honored according to due rite.

sanskrit: tataḥ paramasatkāraṃ sumateḥ prāpya rāghavau uṣya tatra niśām ekāṃ jagmatur mithilāṃ tataḥ
english: Then the two Rāghavas, having received the highest hospitality from Sumati and having spent one night there, departed for Mithilā.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā munayaḥ sarve janakasya purīṃ śubhām sādhu sādhv iti śaṃsanto mithilāṃ samapūjayan
english: Seeing the beautiful city of King Janaka, all the sages praised it, exclaiming "Excellent! Excellent!" and honored Mithilā.

sanskrit: mithilopavane tatra āśramaṃ dṛśya rāghavaḥ purāṇaṃ nirjanaṃ ramyaṃ papraccha munipuṃgavam
english: In the grove of Mithilā, Rāghava, seeing an ancient hermitage, deserted yet lovely, asked the foremost of sages about it.

sanskrit: śrīmadāśramasaṃkāśaṃ kiṃ nv idaṃ munivarjitam śrotum icchāmi bhagavan kasyāyaṃ pūrva āśramaḥ
english: What is this that has the appearance of a splendid hermitage yet is abandoned by sages? I wish to hear, O blessed one, whose former āśrama this was.

sanskrit: tac chrutā rāghaveṇoktaṃ vākyaṃ vākyaviśāradaḥ pratyuvāca mahātejā viśvamitro mahāmuniḥ
english: Having heard the words spoken by Rāghava, the great sage Viśvāmitra, eloquent in speech and of great splendor, replied.

sanskrit: hanta te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇu tattvena rāghava yasyaitad āśramapadaṃ śaptaṃ kopān mahātmanā
english: Come, I shall tell you — listen to the truth, O Rāghava: this hermitage site was cursed in wrath by that great-souled one to whom it belonged.

sanskrit: gautamasya naraśreṣṭha pūrvam āsīn mahātmanaḥ āśramo divyasaṃkāśaḥ surair api supūjitaḥ
english: O best of men, this was formerly the hermitage of the great-souled Gautama, divine in its appearance, worshipped even by the gods.

sanskrit: sa ceha tapa ātiṣṭhad ahalyāsahitaḥ purā varṣapūgāny anekāni rājaputra mahāyaśāḥ
english: Here he dwelt performing austerities together with Ahalyā in former times, for many accumulations of years, O prince, that one of great renown.

sanskrit: tasyāntaraṃ viditvā tu sahasrākṣaḥ śacīpatiḥ muniveṣadharo 'halyām idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Discerning an opportunity when Gautama was absent, the thousand-eyed Indra, lord of Śacī, disguised in the sage's form, spoke these words to Ahalyā.

sanskrit: ṛtukālaṃ pratīkṣante nārthinaḥ susamāhite saṃgamaṃ tv aham icchāmi tvayā saha sumadhyame
english: Those who desire do not wait for the proper season, O composed one — I desire union with you, O slender-waisted one.

sanskrit: muniveṣaṃ sahasrākṣaṃ vijñāya raghunandana matiṃ cakāra durmedhā devarājakutūhalāt
english: Recognizing the thousand-eyed Indra in the sage's disguise, O delight of the Raghu line, the foolish-minded Ahalyā resolved to do it out of curiosity about the king of the gods.

sanskrit: athābravīt suraśreṣṭhaṃ kṛtārthenāntarātmanā kṛtārtho 'si suraśreṣṭha gaccha śīghram itaḥ prabho ātmānaṃ māṃ ca deveśa sarvadā rakṣa mānadaḥ
english: Then, her inner self satisfied and her purpose fulfilled, she spoke to that foremost of gods: "Your purpose is accomplished, O foremost of gods — depart quickly from here, O lord; protect both yourself and me always, O lord of the gods, O giver of honor."

sanskrit: indras tu prahasan vākyam ahalyām idam abravīt suśroṇi parituṣṭo 'smi gamiṣyāmi yathāgatam
english: Smiling, Indra spoke these words to Ahalyā: "O fair-hipped one, I am fully satisfied; I shall depart as I came."

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃgamya tu tayā niścakrāmoṭajāt tataḥ sa saṃbhramāt tvaran rāma śaṅkito gautamaṃ prati
english: Having thus lain with her, he departed from the cottage, O Rāma, hurrying in agitation and fearing Gautama.

sanskrit: gautamaṃ sa dadarśātha praviśantaṃ mahāmunim devadānavadurdharṣaṃ tapobalasamanvitam tīrthodakapariklinnaṃ dīpyamānam ivānalam gṛhītasamidhaṃ tatra sakuśaṃ munipuṅgavam
english: He then saw the great sage Gautama entering — that foremost of sages who was irresistible to gods and demons alike, endowed with the strength of austerity, wet from the waters of a sacred ford, blazing like a fire, holding sacrificial faggots and kuśa grass.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā surapatis trasto viṣaṇṇavadano 'bhavat
english: Seeing him, the lord of the gods was terrified and his face fell.

sanskrit: atha dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaṃ muniveṣadharaṃ muniḥ durvṛttaṃ vṛttasaṃpanno roṣād vacanam abravīt
english: Then the sage, seeing the thousand-eyed Indra disguised as a sage — himself of upright conduct seeing this one of evil conduct — spoke in anger.

sanskrit: mama rūpaṃ samāsthāya kṛtavān asi durmate akartavyam idaṃ yasmād viphalas tvaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: "Having assumed my form, O evil-minded one, you have done what ought not to be done — therefore you shall become bereft of your testicles."

sanskrit: gautamenaivam uktasya saroṣeṇa mahātmanā petatur vṛṣaṇau bhūmau sahasrākṣasya tatkṣaṇāt
english: The very instant that the great-souled Gautama spoke thus in anger, the two testicles of the thousand-eyed Indra fell to the ground.

sanskrit: tathā śaptvā sa vai śakraṃ bhāryām api ca śaptavān iha varṣasahasrāṇi bahūni tvaṃ nivatsyasi
english: Having thus cursed Indra, he also cursed his wife: "Here you shall dwell for many thousands of years."

sanskrit: vāyubhakṣā nirāhārā tapyantī bhasmaśāyinī adṛśyā sarvabhūtānām āśrame 'smin nivatsyasi
english: "Living on air, without food, mortifying yourself, lying in ashes, invisible to all beings, you shall dwell in this hermitage."

sanskrit: yadā caitad vanaṃ ghoraṃ rāmo daśarathātmajaḥ āgamiṣyati durdharṣas tadā pūtā bhaviṣyasi
english: "When Rāma, the invincible son of Daśaratha, comes to this dreadful forest, then you shall be purified."

sanskrit: tasyātithyaṃ ca durvṛtte lobhamohavivarjitā matsakāśe mudā yuktā svaṃ vapur dhārayiṣyasi
english: "Offering hospitality to him, O sinful woman, freed from greed and delusion, joyful in my presence, you shall resume your own form."

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahātejā gautamo duṣṭacāriṇīm imam āśramam utsṛjya siddhacāraṇasevite himavacchikhare ramye tapas tepe mahātapāḥ
english: Having spoken thus to her who had behaved wickedly, the greatly splendid Gautama, that great ascetic, abandoned this hermitage and performed austerities on a beautiful peak of the Himālayas, frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: aphalas tu tataḥ śakro devān agnipurogamān abravīt trastavadanaḥ sarṣisaṃghān sacāraṇān
english: Then Indra, now bereft of his testicles, with a frightened face, spoke to the gods led by Agni, together with the hosts of sages and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: kurvatā tapaso vighnaṃ gautamasya mahātmanaḥ krodham utpādya hi mayā surakāryam idaṃ kṛtam
english: "By creating an obstacle to the austerities of the great-souled Gautama, by provoking his anger, I have accomplished this deed for the benefit of the gods."

sanskrit: aphalo 'smi kṛtas tena krodhāt sā ca nirākṛtā śāpamokṣeṇa mahatā tapo 'syāpahṛtaṃ mayā
english: "By him in his fury I have been rendered without testicles, and she has been repudiated; by my great curse she has been set free from it — her accumulated austerity I have taken from her."

sanskrit: tan māṃ suravarāḥ sarve sarṣisaṃghāḥ sacāraṇāḥ surasāhyakaraṃ sarve saphalaṃ kartum arhatha
english: "Therefore, O best of gods, all of you together with the hosts of sages and Cāraṇas, who perform deeds helpful to the gods — you all ought to restore me to wholeness."

sanskrit: śatakrator vacaḥ śrutvā devāḥ sāgnipurogamāḥ pitṛdevān upetyāhuḥ saha sarvair marudgaṇaiḥ
english: Hearing the words of Śatakratu, the gods led by Agni, together with all the hosts of Maruts, approached the deity of the ancestors and said:

sanskrit: ayaṃ meṣaḥ savṛṣaṇaḥ śakro hy avṛṣaṇaḥ kṛtaḥ meṣasya vṛṣaṇau gṛhya śakrāyāśu prayacchata
english: "This ram here has its testicles, while Indra has been rendered without his — take the ram's testicles and quickly give them to Indra."

sanskrit: aphalas tu kṛto meṣaḥ parāṃ tuṣṭiṃ pradāsyati bhavatāṃ harṣaṇārthāya ye ca dāsyanti mānavāḥ
english: "The ram, rendered without its testicles, shall bestow the highest satisfaction upon you; and those humans who will offer it to you for your delight shall also be benefited."

sanskrit: agnes tu vacanaṃ śrutvā pitṛdevāḥ samāgatāḥ utpāṭya meṣavṛṣaṇau sahasrākṣe nyavedayan
english: Hearing the words of Agni, the ancestors assembled, and having extracted the ram's testicles, presented them to the thousand-eyed Indra.

sanskrit: tadā prabhṛti kākutstha pitṛdevāḥ samāgatāḥ aphalān bhuñjate meṣān phalais teṣām ayojayan
english: From that time onward, O descendant of Kākutstha, the ancestors when assembled partake of rams without their testicles — and they ordained that those animals' testicles be the fruit offered to them.

sanskrit: indras tu meṣavṛṣaṇas tadā prabhṛti rāghava gautamasya prabhāvena tapasaś ca mahātmanaḥ
english: And Indra, from that time onward, O Rāghava, has had the testicles of a ram — by the power of the great-souled Gautama's austerity.

sanskrit: tadāgaccha mahāteja āśramaṃ puṇyakarmaṇaḥ tārayaināṃ mahābhāgām ahalyāṃ devarūpiṇīm
english: Therefore now come, O one of great splendor, to the hermitage of that one of holy deeds — liberate this illustrious Ahalyā, who is like a goddess in form.

sanskrit: viśvāmitravacaḥ śrutvā rāghavaḥ sahalakṣmaṇaḥ viśvāmitraṃ puraskṛtya āśramaṃ praviveśa ha
english: Hearing the words of Viśvāmitra, Rāghava together with Lakṣmaṇa, placing Viśvāmitra at their head, entered the hermitage.

sanskrit: dadarśa ca mahābhāgāṃ tapasā dyotitaprabhām lokair api samāgamya durnirīkṣyāṃ surāsuraiḥ
english: And he beheld the illustrious Ahalyā, her radiance blazing with austerity, impossible to gaze upon even for gods and demons assembled together.

sanskrit: prayatnān nirmitāṃ dhātrā divyāṃ māyāmayīm iva dhūmenābhiparītāṅgīṃ pūrṇacandraprabhām iva
english: She was like one fashioned with care by the Creator as a divine illusion, her body enveloped in smoke yet shining like the full moon.

sanskrit: satuṣārāvṛtāṃ sābhrāṃ pūrṇacandraprabhām iva madhye 'mbhaso durādharṣāṃ dīptāṃ sūryaprabhām iva
english: She was veiled in frost and clouds, like the splendor of the full moon, difficult to approach in the midst of waters, blazing like the brilliance of the sun.

sanskrit: sa hi gautamavākyena durnirīkṣyā babhūva ha trayāṇām api lokānāṃ yāvad rāmasya darśanam
english: For by Gautama's words she had become impossible to behold by the three worlds, until Rāma's sight should fall upon her.

sanskrit: rāghavau tu tatas tasyāḥ pādau jagṛhatus tadā smarantī gautamavacaḥ pratijagrāha sā ca tau
english: Then the two Rāghavas clasped her feet; remembering Gautama's words, she received them.

sanskrit: pādyam arghyaṃ tathātithyaṃ cakāra susamāhitā pratijagrāha kākutstho vidhidṛṣṭena karmaṇā
english: Composed in mind, she performed the rites of water for the feet, the water of honor, and the guest-offering; the descendant of Kākutstha received them according to the prescribed rites.

sanskrit: puṣpavṛṣṭir mahaty āsīd devadundubhinisvanaiḥ gandharvāpsarasāṃ cāpi mahān āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: There was a great shower of flowers accompanied by the sound of divine drums, and there was a great gathering of Gandharvas and Apsarases.

sanskrit: sādhu sādhv iti devās tām ahalyāṃ samapūjayan tapobalaviśuddhāṅgīṃ gautamasya vaśānugām
english: Crying "Excellent! Excellent!", the gods honored Ahalyā, whose body had been purified by the power of austerity, who was now devoted to Gautama's will.

sanskrit: gautamo 'pi mahātejā ahalyāsahitaḥ sukhī rāmaṃ saṃpūjya vidhivat tapas tepe mahātapāḥ
english: And the greatly splendid Gautama, that great ascetic, happy with Ahalyā, duly honored Rāma and resumed his austerities.

sanskrit: rāmo 'pi paramāṃ pūjāṃ gautamasya mahāmuneḥ sakāśād vidhivat prāpya jagāma mithilāṃ tataḥ
english: And Rāma, having duly received the highest honor from the great sage Gautama, then departed for Mithilā.
